deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from the previous page, not shown here). An isotropic homogeneous body is considered in which the temperature depends, besides time, on a single spatial function V. After reparametrisation V can be taken harmonic. Write (p,q,r) = grad V, so curl-free: q_z = r_y, r_x = p_z, p_y = q_x, and ΔV = p_x + q_y + r_z = 0. Riemann splits by the rank of the Jacobian of (p,q,r). Case 2 is rank 2. There he uses the Legendre transform s = V − xp − yq − zr, with ds = −x dp − y dq − z dr. After proving r = 0 (a, b constants, axis rotated), s = s(p,q) is harmonic in (p,q). From the earlier isothermality condition he takes s = ψ(m) + p·χ(β), with m = p²+q² and β = q/p.

Derivation of the separated equations [my check, previous page]:
- Δ_{p,q} ψ(m) = 4ψ' + 4mψ''.
- Δ_{p,q}[pχ(q/p)] = (1+β²)χ''(β)/p.
- Since p = √m/√(1+β²), harmonicity gives √m(4ψ'+4mψ'') + (1+β²)^{3/2} χ''(β) = 0.
- This separates into √m(4ψ'+4mψ'') = κ and χ''(β) = κ/(1+β²)^{3/2}. The sign of the second is wrong; see errors.

THIS PAGE.
(i) Complete integral: χ(β) = κ√(1+β²) + a + bβ, with a, b arbitrary. The marginal computation d/dβ[β/√(1+β²)] = 1/√(1+β²) − β²/(1+β²)^{3/2} = (1+β²)^{−3/2} checks this.

(ii) Coordinates from x = −s_p, y = −s_q:
- −x = 2pψ'(m) + χ − βχ', and χ − βχ' = κ/√(1+β²) + a.
- −y = 2qψ'(m) + χ', and χ' = κβ/√(1+β²) + b.
- With p = √m/√(1+β²) and q = β√m/√(1+β²):
  x + a = −(2√m ψ'(m) + κ)/√(1+β²)
  y + b = −(2√m ψ'(m) + κ)β/√(1+β²)
- Hence (x+a)² + (y+b)² = (2√m ψ'(m) + κ)².

So |grad V|² = m, and therefore V, is constant on circles about (−a,−b), independent of z. The isothermal surfaces are coaxial circular cylinders ('cylindri eodem axe praediti'; margin variant: 'rotatione orti circum eundem axem').
[My addition] Solving the ψ-equation with the correct sign gives 2√m ψ' + κ = 2C/√m. So the radius R = 2C/|grad V|, i.e. V = const·log R, the logarithmic potential, as it must be.

(iii) Case 3 (rank 1): p, q, r are functions ψ1, ψ2, ψ3 of a single ρ.
- The curl-free conditions give ψ_i'ρ_j = ψ_j'ρ_i, i.e. (ψ1',ψ2',ψ3') ∥ grad ρ.
- Then Δ = 0 becomes Σψ_i'ρ_{x_i} = 0, i.e. λ|grad ρ|² = 0.
- So this is impossible unless everything is constant. In modern terms: a symmetric rank-1 Hessian λvvᵀ with zero trace vanishes.

(iv) Case 4: p, q, r constant. V is linear and the isotherms are parallel planes.
Together with the earlier cases, the admissible isothermal families are (concentric spheres, case 1, presumably), coaxial cylinders and parallel planes.

(v) The general Paris question: temperature depending on time and TWO variables; case n = 1.
- The quadratic form, in Gauss notation (0 0 c; a' b' c'), is 2c' dα dβ + 2b' dα dγ + 2a' dβ dγ + c dγ². Here a', b' are linear in γ and c' is independent of γ.
- Its determinant det[[0,c',b'],[c',0,a'],[b',a',c]] = 2a'b'c' − c c'² must be constant.
- The adjoint form is −(a'dα + b'dβ − c'dγ)² + 2(2a'b' − cc') dα dβ. Since det = c'(2a'b' − cc') is constant and c' is free of γ, 2a'b' − cc' is free of γ.
- A substitution γ̃ = λ(α,β)γ + μ(α,β) brings it (up to overall sign/factor) to (a dα + c dγ)² + 2m dα dβ, with a linear in γ and c, m independent of γ. [My filling] Choose (log λ)_β = −b1/c' and μ_β = −b0λ/c', where b' = b0 + b1γ. This kills the dβ term inside the square and leaves the dα dβ term untouched.
- Remaining task (carried out on the next page with the curvature expressions (ιι',ι''ι''') = 0): find when this form is equivalent to one with constant coefficients, i.e. dx² + dy² + dz².
errors: Sign slip (previous page, carried here): harmonicity requires χ''(β) = −κ/(1+β²)^{3/2} if √m(4ψ'+4mψ'') = +κ. Riemann takes χ'' = +κ/(1+β²)^{3/2} and integrates to κ√(1+β²). The slip is harmless: the κ√m term of s can be absorbed into ψ(m), and the cylinder conclusion only uses that the radius depends on m alone.
The κ in χ is in fact redundant: pχ(β) = κ√(p²+q²) + ap + bq, so s is a radial function of (p,q) plus a linear term. Riemann does not remark this.

Notational reuse: the integration constants a, b on this page clash with a, b of r = ap + bq on the previous page (those were set to zero). Later, a and c in (a dα + c dγ)² are reused again with new meanings.

The step 'facile perspicitur' (a linear change of γ yields the form (a dα + c dγ)² + 2m dα dβ) is unproved in the text. It is correct, but it requires quadratures in β (λ, μ functions of α, β) and an overall sign change of the adjoint form.
Case 3 argument is correct but terse: it should say the parallelism forces the proportionality factor times |grad ρ|² to vanish.

results.what: Rank-2 (cylindrical) case: via the Legendre transform of a harmonic V with |grad V| constant on level sets, the isotherms are coaxial circular cylinders, (x+a)²+(y+b)² = F(|grad V|²).
results.modern_name: Classification of isoparametric (isothermal-family) surfaces in R³: planes, coaxial cylinders, concentric spheres; cylinder case
results.usually_credited_to: Lamé (isothermal surfaces, 1830s-1859) for the physical problem; full classification of isoparametric surfaces in R³ to Laura (1918) / Somigliana (1919), general R^n to Levi-Civita (1937) and B. Segre (1938)

results.what: Rank-1 Hessian of a harmonic function must vanish (curl-free plus divergence-free with a one-parameter gradient implies constant gradient)
results.modern_name: trace-free symmetric rank-one matrix is zero

results.what: Reduction for the two-variable (n=1) case: quadratic form with zero α², β² coefficients, its determinant and adjoint form, and normalisation to (a dα + c dγ)² + 2m dα dβ before applying the flatness criterion
results.modern_name: Normal form of a metric prior to testing vanishing Riemann curvature (flatness); Riemann's 1861 Paris Commentatio

results.what: Integral χ = κ√(1+β²) + a + bβ of χ'' = κ(1+β²)^{-3/2}

deep.surprise_reason: The page is part of the drafts of the known Paris-prize Commentatio, so the n=1 reduction is expected material. The interesting part is the explicit proof that, for temperature depending on time and one spatial variable, only planes, coaxial cylinders (and spheres) can be isotherms. That is the R³ classification of isoparametric surfaces usually credited to Laura/Somigliana/Segre (1918-38), and here it is done via a Legendre transform. Whether this detail appears in the published Commentatio or was known (e.g. to Lamé) is uncertain, so the score is moderate.

transcription_corrections: 'λ(β) = κ√(1+β²) + a + b.β' should read 'χ(β) = κ√(1+β²) + a + bβ' (the function χ from the previous page).
'2ψ(u)√u + κ' (three occurrences) should read '2ψ'(m)√m + κ'. The variable is m = p²+q², and the derivative ψ' is needed.
The struck-out right-hand side in (x+a)²+(y+b)² is an earlier version, roughly (2ψ'(m)+κ)², replaced by (2ψ'(m)√m + κ)².

Quadratic form in Gauss notation: the upper row is (0 0 c), not (c c c''). The determinant matrix is [[0,c',b'],[c',0,a'],[b',a',c]] (zeros on the first two diagonal places), consistent with the value 2a'b'c' − cc'c'.
'cylindri eadem axi' is Riemann's (ungrammatical) 'eodem axe'. The margin variant reads 'rotatione orti circum eandem axem' and is an alternative wording, not a separate note.
The insertion over 'gaudentes' in 'Casum tertium... praediti' belongs to line 'cylindri eodem axe praediti'. At the bottom of the page 'praeditam' is an alternative to 'gaudentem'.
'occurrere {+evenire+}' marks 'evenire' as a pencilled alternative to 'occurrere'.
